title: asymmetric-page-throttler-and-occupancy-reclaimer
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Adds asymmetric page throttling and an occupancy-based reclaimer to reduce fragmentation-related memory pressure and smooth spill bursts; includes rollout knobs and default-off flags for private deployments.
description:
Motivation: production workloads with skewed tenant footprints were triggering large, synchronous spill operations and accelerated fragmentation that degraded tail latency. This PR introduces two coordinated subsystems: 1) an Asymmetric Page Throttler that applies differentiated service to page classes (hot, warm, cold) and enforces per-tenant spill pacing via a lightweight token-bucket metronome; 2) an Occupancy Reclaimer that opportunistically compacts small-object dominated pages and reclaims slack in-place without immediate spill. Both aim to reduce instantaneous memory pressure, smooth spillback to external storage, and improve end-to-end latency stability.

Design summary: the throttler tracks per-page buckets (metadata only) and maintains a lease counter used by the scheduler to decide when to evict/mark pages for spill. Rather than treating all spill candidates equally, the scheduler lowers priority for warm pages with high fragmentation but low live occupancy and prioritizes cold pages that will substantially reduce resident set. The occupancy reclaimer samples page slots and performs bounded micro-compaction cycles: if >60% of slots are small-fragment allocations and compaction is estimated to free >= X bytes, the page is compacted in-place. A Spillback Metronome paces outgoing spill writes to the object store to avoid bursts; rate is tenant-configurable and adapts to observed write latency.

Implementation notes: changes are localized to src/kv/(allocator.rs, scheduler.rs, evictor.rs, reclaimer.rs) and runtime knobs in config/kv.yaml. New metrics exposed: kv.throttler.tokens_{tenant}, kv.reclaimer.compactions, kv.spill.metronome_rate, kv.page.occupancy_histogram. A runtime flag --kv-opportunistic-compact defaults to false on Private builds to avoid surprises in highly-regulated environments.

Checklist:
- [x] Design review (ENG-4821)
- [x] Unit tests for allocator heuristics and reclaimer
- [x] Integration test simulating tenant spike and spill smoothing
- [x] Benchmarks: 99th latency improvement under synthetic skew
- [x] Docs and config examples added to docs/ops/kv-throttling.md
- [x] Rollout plan added to REDWOOD-OPS playbook

Performance: on internal perf-lab with a 10-tenant skewed workload (one tenant generating 60% of requests), we observed: median latency +2% (noise), p95 reduced by ~18%, p99 reduced by ~26%, and total spill write IOPS variance reduced by ~45%. Memory reclaimed from compaction averaged 12% of RSS in hotspots, avoiding 3 full node-level spill events during a 30-minute stress window.

Rollback and rollout: feature gated behind kv.asymmetric_throttler.enabled and kv.opportunistic_compact.enabled. Rollout strategy: enable throttler in canary (10% traffic) for 24h, monitor kv.spill.metronome_rate and p99 latency; then enable reclaimer in staged canary with strict cost limits for 48h.

Related: follows work in ENG-4130 (spillback smoothing) and complements existing kv-eviction heuristics by focusing on occupancy and fragmentation rather than simple LRU weight.

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to scheduler.rs change where lease accounting interacts with batching paths; small change in protocol for continuous batching: when lease tokens are exhausted, batches are allowed to complete but new batch assignment defers until tokens refill (ensures request-level tail bounds).

review_comments: Ravi Patel: Nice separation of concerns. Question: how does the metronome interact with burst capacity for Dedicated nodes? Can we allow short bursts when tenant SLA permits?
Maya Thompson: answered - metronome allows a burst window configurable via kv.spill.metronome_burst_tokens, default 2x sustained rate. Dedicated plans can set it higher via tenant profile.
Lindsey Moore: found a potential race in scheduler.rs when token refill and batch assignment overlap; suggested adding a CAS on lease counter.
Maya Thompson: addressed with atomic fetch_add/fetch_sub and added unit test kv_lease_race_test (ci/kv_unit_tests.yml).
Jun Park: please add a stress test that validates compaction doesn't exceed CPU budget on small nodes.
Maya Thompson: added cpu-budgeted_compactor mode and updated integration test (tests/integration/kv_spill_stress.py) to assert CPU < 40% during compaction phase.

backwards_compatibility: No breaking API changes to client-facing APIs. Config defaults are conservative; operators must opt-in for aggressive compaction.
